This version changes the Shell core, so updating from the app asks for administrator approval once.

Many of these come from RubicBG's ReShell (shared with his permission). Thank you, RubicBG.

**New things you can write in your menu files**
- `str.fmt` fills values into a text: `str.fmt('{0} of {1}', sel.count, 10)` gives "2 of 10". `str.format` does the same; before, it returned nothing.
- `app.set`, `app.get`, `app.exists` and `app.remove` remember a value between menus, even after a restart. For example `cmd=app.set('fav', sel.dir)` on one item and `cmd=app.get('fav')` on another gives you a folder you can come back to. Values are kept for your Windows account only.
- `path.file.save_box` shows a Save As box and gives back the path that was chosen, for example `path.file.save_box('Text|*.txt', user.desktop, 'list.txt')`.
- `path.dir.box` can start in a folder and show your own title: `path.dir.box(sel.dir, 'Pick a folder')`.
- `path.absolute('..\backup')` and `path.relative(sel.path)` turn a path into a full one, or into one that starts from the folder you right-clicked in. Before, both returned nothing.
- `io.move` can move a file to another drive, and takes an optional third value to replace a file that is already there.
- `input()` can show a drop-down list to pick from: `input('Size', 'Pick a size', '', ['Small', 'Medium', 'Large'])`. `input.selected` tells you which item was picked.
- `indexof()` accepts a number as the place to put an item when nothing matches.
- `key.return` works as a name for the Enter key, as the docs already said.
- `appx()` can tell you more about a Microsoft Store app: `appx('WindowsTerminal', 'executable')` gives its program file, and `appx.logo`, `appx.square44` and `appx.square150` give its pictures, so an item can show the app's own icon.
- `sel.lnk.args` gives the arguments of a shortcut, and `sel.lnk.raw` gives its target and arguments together. `path.lnk.args` and `path.lnk.raw` do the same for any shortcut path.
- `sys.power.battery` gives the battery charge, for example `item(title='Battery: ' + sys.power.battery + '%' where=sys.power.battery >= 0)`. `sys.power.is_charging` and `sys.power.is_ac` tell you how the PC is powered.
- `sys.memory`, `sys.memory.free` and `sys.memory.total` show how much memory is in use and free. `sys.cpu.count` gives the number of processors Windows sees.
- `sys.screen.width`, `sys.screen.height` and `sys.screen.count` describe your screens. `sys.lang.full` gives the Windows display language by name, such as "English (United States)".
- `sel.drop` gives the folder you drop files into when you drag them with the right mouse button, so an item in that menu can work with the place you dropped them. It works in the file list of a File Explorer window and on the desktop, and is empty anywhere else.
- `user.groups` lists the Windows groups you are in, and `user.groups('Remote Desktop Users')` tells you whether you are in one. You can also name a group by its SID, such as `'S-1-5-32-544'`, which works whatever language Windows is in. Administrators only counts when File Explorer runs as administrator.
- `command.refresh(2)` refreshes the folder and also rebuilds the Windows icon cache, for icons that show wrong.
- `sel.item` gives the path of the item a command is running for, and `type.cd` is another name for `type.dvd`.
- New, and off unless you turn it on: `settings.filemanagers` lets Shell's menu see the files you right-click in other file managers, such as Total Commander, XYplorer, Double Commander and Everything. List the programs, for example `filemanagers = ['totalcmd64', 'xyplorer']`, and let Shell's menu into them in `exclude.where`. It has had little testing so far, so tell us how it goes. The [Settings](https://abdullah-masood-05.github.io/Shell/configuration/settings/#filemanagers) page explains it.
- `menu='/'` on an item inside one of your submenus puts it in the main menu, as it already did for `modify()`.
- In `modify()`, `menu='/'` now also keeps an item in the main menu: the rules after it don't move it into a submenu. So a rule can take back a move that a later file, such as the bundled `modify.nss`, makes.
- `run`, `exec`, `launch`, `cmd` and `shell` take up to six values: the file, its arguments, how to open it (such as `'runas'` or `'open'`), the folder it starts in, how its window shows, and whether to wait for it to close. For example `run('cmd.exe', '/c ipconfig /flushdns', 'runas', null, cmd.hidden, 1)`. The older forms still work, and the folder is still the one you right-clicked in unless you give another.
- `clipboard.is_files` tells you when files were copied or cut in File Explorer, and `clipboard.files` gives their paths: `clipboard.files[0]` is the first, `clipboard.files.count` says how many, and `clipboard.files.name(', ')` lists their names.
- `this.tip` and `this.key` give an item's tip and the shortcut text at its right. `this.parent.title`, `.name`, `.tip`, `.key`, `.id` and `.count` describe the submenu the item is in, so a `modify()` rule can pick items by the menu they are in. Before, `this.parent.title` gave a number.
- Your menu files can read the theme in use: `theme.name`, `theme.font` and `theme.font.size`, `theme.border.radius`, `theme.item.radius`, `theme.shadow.size`, `theme.separator.color` and more, so your items can match the menu. The [Themes](https://abdullah-masood-05.github.io/Shell/configuration/themes/#read) page lists them all.
- `wnd.is_dialog` is true when you right-click inside an Open or Save As box, and `command.navigate` now works there too: it opens the folder in the box and keeps the file name you typed. For example `item(title='Desktop' where=wnd.is_dialog cmd=command.navigate(user.desktop))`.
- `path.dir.boxl` shows the older Browse For Folder box, with the folders as a tree, and gives back the folder you picked: `path.dir.boxl(sel.dir, 'Pick a folder')`.

**Fixes**
- `key.ctrl()` is true while Ctrl is held. Before, it never was.
- `col=` no longer removes the `keys=` text of the same item.
- `color.rgb(255, 0, 0)` and `color(255, 0, 0)` give red. Red and blue were swapped and the color was see-through.
- `color.random` gives a random visible color. Before, it was always black and see-through.
- `type.file`, `type.dir` and the other `type.*` names give their numbers, and `path.type('C:\Windows')` tells you what a path is. A snippet that compared these could never match before.
- `sel.type(5)` with fewer items selected no longer crashes Explorer.
- `theme.item.back.select` and the other `theme.item` color names give the theme's colors. `theme.item.border.normal` and `theme.item.border.select` are new.
- `cmd.show`, `cmd.visible` and `shell.maximized` and its friends give their values. Before, they returned nothing.
- `sys.is7orgreater`, `sys.is8orgreater` and `sys.is81orgreater` are true on Windows 10 and 11.
- The config check accepts `sys.datetime.s`, `.h`, `.d`, `.dw` and `.m`, which already worked in menus.
- `this.type` gives 0 for an item, 1 for a menu and 2 for a separator for the items you add too, as documented. If you worked around the old numbers, check those lines.
- `str.split('a,,b', ',')` gives the two parts "a" and "b". Before, it gave one part, "a,b".
- `reg.get` and `reg.set` handle binary values, and `reg.keys` and `reg.values` no longer cut long names short.
- `var.name[0]` picks one part of a `var` value, as `$name[0]` does, and asking for a place past the end of a text gives nothing instead of garbage.
- A round (radial) gradient in a theme is centred across the menu.
- An item inside one of your submenus with `menu=` shows in the menu it names even when you haven't opened its own submenu first.
- In `run('app.exe', 'arguments', cmd.hidden)` and `shell(file, arguments, verb, cmd.maximized)`, the window value now sets how the window shows. Before, it only decided whether to wait for the program.
- A PowerShell script of several lines in `cmd-ps=` or `cmd-pwsh=` runs in full. Before, only its first line ran. Switches such as `-NoExit` can still go before the script.
- A right-click on the taskbar checks where you clicked once instead of twice, so its menu opens a little sooner.
- `modify(find='copy' menu='Tools')` works when Tools is one of your menus with `expanded=1`. Before, the Windows item left its place and showed nowhere.
- Hiding one of your menus no longer hides the items you moved out of it. For example, after moving Copy path out of File manage to the main menu, turning File manage off keeps Copy path in the main menu.
- Register Server in File manage shows only for .dll and .ocx files. Before, it also showed for Word files (.docx), because `find='.ocx'` matches any extension that contains "ocx". Write `find='."ocx"'` to match one extension exactly. Copy file contents, Run with arguments, Extract to folder and Verify Checksum file had the same mistake and are fixed too. Thanks to Bits-Bytes-354 for the report.
- A command that makes a folder with `io.dir.create`, or a file with `io.file.create(..., true)`, no longer makes File Explorer freeze and restart, along with the taskbar and desktop. Shell now selects and renames the new item from File Explorer's own window, and only when it was made in the folder you right-clicked in. A folder made somewhere else, like your own links folder, is just created. Thanks to TiAmo-KO for the report and the careful analysis (#8).

**Settings app**
- Menu map can move and reorder your own Shell items too, such as Empty Recycle Bin in System. Pick a menu under Move to, a place under Place in this menu, or use the arrows on the item's row (Alt+Up and Alt+Down work too).
- Move to on the Menu map starts with Main menu, for Windows items and your own: it takes an item out of a submenu, or keeps one such as Create shortcut out of More options.
- The Menu map's File samples now include an application (.exe) and a shortcut (.lnk), which show Troubleshoot compatibility. Items a program adds only inside File Explorer, such as Scan with Microsoft Defender on some PCs, can be added by their title to hide, rename or move them.
- The app is available in Arabic, reviewed and corrected by kaser4. Preferences > Language lists it as العربية, and Auto picks it when Windows is in Arabic.
- Version numbers show in the right order in Arabic: 2.3.0-beta.3, not beta.3-2.3.0.
- Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+X, Ctrl+A and Ctrl+Z work in the app's text boxes with an Arabic, Russian or other non-Latin keyboard layout too.
- The Menu map's side panel can change an item's icon. Pick an .ico, .png or .svg file or a program with Browse, or type a glyph such as `image.mdl(\uE8C8)`. Remove icon takes it away. It works for your own items and for Windows items.
- Ctrl+S saves on every page again, whatever has focus. On Context Menus, Menu Builder and in the Menu map's Edit code it did nothing before.
- The Snippets page's preview looks like the real menu now: full size on your wallpaper, with the snippet's submenu open and a label saying what to right-click. The snippet's items have a thin outline and the items already in your menu are faded, instead of the blue marks. While it loads you see the outline of a menu, and a snippet that only changes other items says so.

**Snippets**
- New on the app's Snippets page: *Play in MPC-BE*, from RubicBG. It adds *Open in MPC* to video and music files, and to folders that have them. Hold Shift to add them to the MPC-BE playlist instead. It needs MPC-BE from the Microsoft Store.
- Also new on the Snippets page: *Quick tools*. It copies details about your PC (screen, memory, processors, battery, language), keeps a folder bookmark you can open from any right-click, and copies a path with forward slashes, in quotes or as a file URL.
- Three more of RubicBG's snippets load now, but they change Windows settings outside Shell (the registry, some as administrator, or file permissions), so they stay off the Snippets page. The rest of his collection loads too, now that `run()` takes six values and `path.dir.boxl` is there.
- The [Snippets page in the docs](https://abdullah-masood-05.github.io/Shell/snippets/) links to his whole collection, and all of it loads now.
- Every snippet on the Snippets page now has its name and description in Arabic and Spanish too, not only in Chinese.

**Docs**
- New and fixed functions are described in the [Functions](https://abdullah-masood-05.github.io/Shell/functions/) pages.
